q: What is the youngest age at which you can get an Alabama learner license?
exp: Any person 15 or older may take the knowledge test and get a Stage I learner license.
src: Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 9; ALEA, Graduated Driver License (alea.gov/dps/driver-license/license-and-id-cards/graduated-driver-license)

q: A 15-year-old with an Alabama learner license is driving. Who may sit in the front seat as the supervisor?
b: A parent, legal guardian, licensed driver 21 or older, or licensed driving instructor
c: Any passenger 21 or older, licensed or not
exp: At 15, the supervisor must be a parent or guardian, a licensed driver at least 21, or a licensed or certified instructor, seated beside you.
src: Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 9, 84; ALEA, Graduated Driver License (alea.gov/dps/driver-license/license-and-id-cards/graduated-driver-license)

q: How long must a driver under 18 hold an Alabama learner license before applying for a Stage II restricted license?
exp: Under 18, you must hold the learner license for at least six months before the road test.
src: Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 10, 84; ALEA, Graduated Driver License (alea.gov/dps/driver-license/license-and-id-cards/graduated-driver-license)

q: Before an Alabama teen can get a Stage II license, what must be shown besides parent consent?
a: Both 50 hours of practice and a driver education course
b: 30 hours of practice, 10 of them at night
d: Either 50 hours of certified practice or an approved driver education course
exp: ALEA accepts either a form certifying at least 50 behind-the-wheel hours or a State Department of Education approved driver ed certificate.
src: ALEA, Graduated Driver License (alea.gov/dps/driver-license/license-and-id-cards/graduated-driver-license); Code of Ala. 32-6-7.2(b)

q: During which hours may an Alabama Stage II driver not drive, unless an exception applies?
exp: Stage II drivers may not drive from midnight to 6 a.m. unless an exception such as work or a parent riding along applies.
src: Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 84; ALEA, Graduated Driver License (alea.gov/dps/driver-license/license-and-id-cards/graduated-driver-license)

q: How many passengers who are not family may an Alabama Stage II driver carry?
exp: A Stage II driver may have no more than one non-family passenger, not counting a parent, guardian or supervising licensed driver 21 or older.
src: Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 84; ALEA, Graduated Driver License (alea.gov/dps/driver-license/license-and-id-cards/graduated-driver-license)

q: An Alabama Stage II driver is cited for breaking a restriction during a stop for speeding. What happens to the restricted period?
a: It starts over from the beginning
c: It is extended by six months or until age 18
d: Nothing changes; only a fine is due
exp: A restriction violation extends the restricted period by six months or until the driver turns 18.
src: Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 84; ALEA, Graduated Driver License (alea.gov/dps/driver-license/license-and-id-cards/graduated-driver-license)

q: What happens when an Alabama Stage II driver is convicted of a second moving violation?
c: A required retest of the knowledge test only
exp: A second moving violation, or an offense worth 4 or more points, brings an automatic 60-day suspension.
src: Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 84; ALEA, Graduated Driver License (alea.gov/dps/driver-license/license-and-id-cards/graduated-driver-license)

q: When can a 17-year-old Alabama driver move from Stage II to an unrestricted Stage III license?
a: After holding the Stage II license six months with no moving violations in the past six months
b: On the 17th birthday, no matter what
c: After one year on the Stage II license
d: Only after passing a second road test
exp: Stage III comes at 17 after at least six months on Stage II with a clean recent record, or at 18.
src: ALEA, Graduated Driver License (alea.gov/dps/driver-license/license-and-id-cards/graduated-driver-license); Code of Ala. 32-6-7.2(f)

q: How much does each attempt at the Alabama knowledge test cost?
exp: The knowledge test fee is $5 for each attempt, and checks are not accepted.
src: Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 11; ALEA, Document Requirements and Fees (alea.gov/dps/driver-license/license-and-id-cards)

q: What agency issues driver licenses in Alabama?
exp: ALEA's Driver License Division issues Alabama licenses.

q: What does the "Y" restriction on an Alabama Class D learner license mean?
a: You may drive only in daylight
b: You may not drive on interstates
d: You may drive only with a qualified supervisor in the seat beside you
exp: The Y restriction shows the holder must have a supervisor occupying the seat beside the driver.
src: Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 9 to 10

q: According to the Alabama manual, who may supervise a learner license holder after the holder's 16th birthday?
a: Any licensed driver in the seat beside the driver
c: Only a licensed driver 25 or older
exp: The manual says that after the 16th birthday, any licensed driver may occupy the seat beside the learner.

q: How long is an Alabama learner license issued at 15 valid?
exp: A learner license issued at 15 is valid for four years and can be renewed once.

q: What birth record must a 15-year-old bring to apply for an Alabama learner license?
b: A photocopy of a birth certificate
c: A certified U.S. birth certificate from a vital records office
d: A school record showing the date of birth
exp: Fifteen-year-old applicants need a certified birth certificate; photocopies are not accepted.
src: Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 8; ALEA, Document Requirements and Fees (alea.gov/dps/driver-license/license-and-id-cards)

q: Which form must a first-time Alabama applicant under 19 present to show school enrollment?
c: A report card signed by a parent
exp: Applicants under 19 present a current DL-1/93 form completed at school, or proof of graduation.
src: Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 8; ALEA, Document Requirements and Fees (alea.gov/dps/driver-license/license-and-id-cards)

q: Which of these documents would ALEA refuse?
a: A birth certificate with white-out on the date of birth
d: A certified copy of a birth certificate
exp: Documents with correction fluid, erasures or alterations on key information are unacceptable.

q: What is the name of Alabama's REAL ID compliant license?
exp: Alabama calls its REAL ID card the STAR ID.

q: How much does ALEA charge to issue a learner license?
exp: The learner license costs $36.25 after the $5 test fee.

q: What extra charge applies when you pay an ALEA fee by credit card?
exp: ALEA accepts cards with a 4 percent convenience fee on the total.

q: Which form of payment does ALEA refuse at the driver license office?
exp: ALEA does not accept checks for testing or license fees.
src: Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 11; ALEA, Graduated Driver License (alea.gov/dps/driver-license/license-and-id-cards/graduated-driver-license)

q: What does the Alabama knowledge test cover?
b: Traffic laws, road signs and safe driving rules from the Alabama Driver Manual
d: Questions on Alabama geography and road names
exp: The test covers traffic laws, signs and safe driving, taken from the manual.

q: Which of these languages is the Alabama knowledge test offered in, besides English?
exp: Foreign language tests include Arabic, Chinese, Farsi, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Russian, Spanish, Thai and Vietnamese.

q: What can an Alabama applicant who cannot read the knowledge test questions request?
exp: Oral exams are available for applicants who cannot read and understand the knowledge test.

q: If you fail the Alabama vision screening, what must you do?
a: Have your eyes examined by a licensed eye specialist and return the report
c: Take the road test with an instructor
exp: A failed screening means an eye specialist's report; if it shows safe vision, you finish your tests.

q: Your vision screening shows you need glasses to drive safely. What follows?
a: You may drive only in daylight
b: Your license is restricted to driving with corrective lenses
c: You cannot be licensed until age 18
exp: If lenses are needed, you must wear them while driving, including on the road test.
src: Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 10 to 11

q: Which of these is an exception to the Alabama Stage II curfew?
a: Driving a friend home from a party
c: Driving to or from your regular job
exp: Going to or from work is one of the listed exceptions.
src: Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 84; ALEA, Graduated Driver License (alea.gov/dps/driver-license/license-and-id-cards/graduated-driver-license)

q: An Alabama Stage II driver may drive after midnight with a licensed driver 21 or older only if:
d: A parent or guardian has consented
exp: A licensed driver 21 or older may supervise after midnight with parental consent.
src: Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 84; ALEA, Graduated Driver License (alea.gov/dps/driver-license/license-and-id-cards/graduated-driver-license)

q: Under current Alabama law, what must a Stage II driver do after a first conviction for breaking a restriction, besides serving the longer restricted period?
d: Surrender the license for one year
exp: A first conviction for breaking a Stage II restriction requires defensive driving school, along with a fine and a six-month extension.
src: Code of Ala. 32-6-7.2(d), (h)(1) (codes.findlaw.com, current to 2024-12-30; Act 2017-442, Deputy Hart Act)

q: What happens to an Alabama Stage II driver convicted a second time of breaking a restriction?
b: Stage II privileges are suspended and the driver goes back to a learner license for six months
c: The license is revoked until age 21
d: The driver must repeat driver education
exp: On a second or later offense, the Stage II privileges are suspended and the driver reverts to a Stage I learner license for six months.
src: Code of Ala. 32-6-7.2(d), (h)(1) (codes.findlaw.com, current to 2024-12-30; Act 2017-442, Deputy Hart Act)

q: To whom do Alabama's graduated license rules NOT apply?
b: A 17-year-old with a Stage II license held three months
c: A 16-year-old who is married and head of a household
exp: The GDL rules do not apply to drivers 18 or older, those married and head of household, or those legally relieved of minority.
src: Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 84; ALEA, Graduated Driver License (alea.gov/dps/driver-license/license-and-id-cards/graduated-driver-license)

q: Who must come with a 16-year-old to the Alabama road test?
exp: A 16-year-old applicant must be accompanied by a parent or guardian.

q: Which equipment does the Alabama examiner check before the road test begins?
a: Brake lights, left and right turn signals and horn
exp: The examiner checks that the car is safe and has brake lights, turn signals and a horn.

q: When may you use a rental car for the Alabama road test?
b: When your name is on the rental agreement as a driver
c: When the rental is less than one week old
exp: A rental car may be used only if the applicant is listed on the rental agreement.

q: On the Alabama road test, how far may you be asked to back up in a straight line?
exp: The road test may include backing about 50 feet slowly and straight while looking to the rear.

q: Which of these causes an automatic fail on the Alabama road test?
a: Asking the examiner to repeat an instruction
b: Stopping smoothly at a yellow light
exp: Crashes, traffic violations, reckless driving and refusing to cooperate fail you at once.

q: An adult of 25 is getting a first Alabama license. Which rule applies?
a: There is no six-month learner hold before the road test
d: They cannot drive after midnight for six months
exp: The GDL rules do not apply at 18 or older, so adults can test without the six-month hold.
src: Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 84; ALEA, Graduated Driver License (alea.gov/dps/driver-license/license-and-id-cards/graduated-driver-license)

q: How long may a new Alabama resident drive on a valid license from their previous state?
exp: A new resident with a valid license from the previous state may drive for 30 days.

q: A new Alabama resident's out-of-state license expired eight months ago. What must they do?
b: Take both the knowledge and road tests
c: Transfer it without a knowledge or road test
d: Start over with a learner license
exp: An out-of-state license expired no more than one year can be transferred without the driver examination.

q: A new resident holds a license from a country that has no license agreement with Alabama. What tests do they take for an Alabama license?
c: No tests if they have an International Driving Permit
d: The vision screening, the knowledge test and the road test
exp: Foreign license holders apply as new drivers and take all tests.
src: University of Alabama ISSS, Transportation, Driving and Driver's Licenses (international.ua.edu); Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 5; ALEA news release, Alabama, Taiwan sign driver license reciprocity agreement (alea.gov/news/alabama-taiwan-sign-driver-license-reciprocity-agreement)

q: Within how many days must you notify ALEA after moving to a new address in Alabama?
exp: You have 30 days to report a new address to the Driver License Division.

q: How long is an Alabama driver license valid?
exp: An Alabama license expires four years after it is issued.

q: In an Alabama construction zone where workers are present, what does a moving violation cost?
a: $250 or double the regular fine, whichever is more
c: $100 or the regular fine, whichever is less
exp: With workers present, a moving violation costs at least $250 or twice the usual fine.
src: Code of Ala. 32-5A-176.1, as amended 2021 (WBRC, June 24, 2021)

q: In Alabama, what must you do when a school safety patrol member holds an official flag in the STOP position?
d: Yield only if children are in the crosswalk
exp: Drivers must stop when a school patrol member displays an official flag in the STOP position.

q: How many points does an Alabama driver receive for failing to obey construction zone markers?
exp: The point schedule assigns 3 points for failing to obey construction or maintenance zone markers.

q: An Alabama school zone sign has flashing yellow lights. When does the lower school speed limit apply?
c: Only when a police officer is present
exp: School zone limits apply during the hours shown or may be shown on a lighted sign with flashing amber lights.

q: Does Alabama's higher work zone fine apply when no workers are present?
a: No, it applies when workers are present
exp: The higher fine applies to moving violations in construction zones where workers are present.
src: Code of Ala. 32-5A-176.1, as amended 2021 (WBRC, June 24, 2021)

q: What do large flashing arrow panels in an Alabama work zone tell you?
a: That the work zone has ended
b: Which lanes to use because part of the road ahead is closed
exp: Flashing or sequencing arrow panels guide drivers into lanes and show that part of the road ahead is closed.

q: In Alabama, when may you turn left on a steady red light?
a: From a one-way street into a one-way street whose traffic flows to your left, after a full stop
b: From any street, after a full stop
d: Only when a green arrow is also lit
exp: Left on red is allowed only from a one-way street onto a one-way street, after stopping and yielding, unless a sign forbids it.
src: Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 60 to 61; Code of Ala. 32-5A-32(3)

q: An Alabama traffic signal is dark because of a power failure. How should you treat the intersection?
a: As a yield sign for all drivers
c: As if you have a green light
d: As a red light that stays red until police arrive
exp: If the traffic light is not working, treat the intersection as a four-way stop.

q: Before turning right on a steady red light in Alabama, you must:
c: Stop completely and yield to pedestrians and cross traffic
d: Wait for the light to turn yellow
exp: Right on red is allowed after a complete stop, yielding to traffic and pedestrians, unless a sign prohibits it.
src: Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 60 to 61

q: In Alabama, what does a steady yellow X over a lane mean?
b: The lane is for buses only
c: Turn left from this lane only
d: You may use the lane, with caution
exp: A steady yellow X permits driving in the lane with caution because of possible hazards.

q: On an Alabama road with two or more lanes your way, you approach a stopped tow truck with flashing amber lights. If you cannot move over safely, what must you do?
a: Slow to at least 15 mph below the posted limit
b: Slow to at least 5 mph below the posted limit
c: Stop until the tow truck leaves
exp: The Move Over law requires leaving the next lane or, if unsafe, slowing to at least 15 mph under the limit.
src: ALEA, Alabama Move Over Act, Code of Ala. 32-5A-58.2 (alea.gov/dps/highway-patrol/alabama-move-over-act); Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 68

q: How close to a stopped Alabama school bus with red lights flashing may you stop?
exp: The Alabama manual tells drivers to stop at least 20 feet from the bus.

q: On a divided Alabama highway with four or more lanes, a school bus stops with red lights flashing on the other side of the median. What must you do?
b: Stop only if children are visible
c: Continue with caution; you do not have to stop
exp: Oncoming traffic on a divided highway of four or more lanes need not stop.
src: Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 61; Code of Ala. 32-5A-154

q: On an undivided Alabama highway with four lanes, a school bus stops with red lights flashing in the opposite lanes. What must you do?
b: Pass only on the far right
c: Stop only on a two-lane road, so keep going
exp: On four to six lane undivided highways, traffic from both directions stops.

q: What is the fine for a first conviction of passing a stopped school bus in Alabama?
exp: A first conviction carries a fine of $150 to $300.

q: How many points does passing a stopped school bus add to an Alabama driving record?
exp: The point schedule assigns 5 points for passing a stopped school bus.

q: In rural Alabama areas, how far ahead of a stop does a school bus usually turn on its yellow warning lights?
exp: Amber lights come on at least 300 feet before stopping in rural areas and at least 100 feet in cities.

q: A second Alabama conviction for passing a stopped school bus adds which license penalty?
exp: A second conviction brings a fine of $300 to $500, community service and a 30-day suspension.

q: On an Alabama two-lane road with a 45 mph limit, you pass a stopped police car with lights flashing. What does the Move Over law require?
a: Move as far from it as you can within your lane and slow to 30 mph or less
b: Cross the center line to give more room
exp: On a two-lane road, move away within your lane and slow to 15 mph below a limit of 25 mph or more.
src: ALEA, Alabama Move Over Act, Code of Ala. 32-5A-58.2 (alea.gov/dps/highway-patrol/alabama-move-over-act); Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 68

q: On an Alabama street with a 20 mph limit, how fast may you pass a stopped emergency vehicle under the Move Over law?
exp: Where the limit is 20 mph or less, drivers must slow to 10 mph.
src: ALEA, Alabama Move Over Act, Code of Ala. 32-5A-58.2 (alea.gov/dps/highway-patrol/alabama-move-over-act); Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 68

q: What is the fine for a first violation of Alabama's Move Over law?
exp: The base fine is $200, then $250 for a second and $300 for a third or later violation.
src: ALEA, Alabama Move Over Act, Code of Ala. 32-5A-58.2 (alea.gov/dps/highway-patrol/alabama-move-over-act)

q: Which of these stopped vehicles is covered by Alabama's Move Over law?
a: A car parked legally at the curb
b: A school bus at a school
c: A delivery van in a driveway
d: A garbage truck collecting trash on the roadside
exp: The law covers emergency vehicles, wreckers, utility and road work vehicles, and garbage or recycling trucks collecting on the roadside.
src: ALEA, Alabama Move Over Act, Code of Ala. 32-5A-58.2 (alea.gov/dps/highway-patrol/alabama-move-over-act)

q: Under Alabama law, how close may you follow a fire truck or ambulance on an emergency run?
exp: Only vehicles on official business may follow within 500 feet of an emergency vehicle on a run.

q: In Alabama, may you drive over an unprotected fire hose?
b: Only when a police officer or fire official tells you to
c: Yes, if it is not spraying water
exp: Do not drive over an unprotected fire hose unless authorized by police or a fire official.

q: You are already in an Alabama roundabout when an ambulance approaches with its siren on. What should you do?
a: Stop at once inside the roundabout
c: Continue to your exit, then pull over
d: Speed up and go around again
exp: If you are in the roundabout, continue to your exit and then pull over; avoid stopping in the circle.

q: In Alabama, how far before a turn must you start signaling?
exp: Signal your intention at least 100 feet before making the turn.

q: Alabama bans turning around on a curve or near the crest of a hill where other drivers cannot see you within how many feet?
exp: Turnarounds are not permitted on curves or near hilltops where you cannot be seen within 500 feet.

q: What is the Alabama hand signal for a right turn?
exp: Right turn: hand and arm extended upward.

q: What is the Alabama hand signal to slow down or stop?
exp: Stop or decrease speed: hand and arm extended downward.

q: You miss your exit on an Alabama freeway. What should you do?
a: Go on to the next exit and come back
b: Stop on the shoulder and back up
d: Slow down in the lane and cut across
exp: If you miss your exit, do not stop, back up or turn around; go to the next exit.

q: Where in Alabama are three-point turns never permitted?
exp: Three-point turns are not permitted on interstates, on curves or near hilltops with limited sight.

q: What is Alabama's speed limit in an urban district when no other limit is posted?
exp: The statutory limit in an urban district is 30 mph.
src: Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 60; Code of Ala. 32-5A-171

q: What following gap does the Alabama Driver Manual teach for normal conditions?
exp: The manual teaches the two-second rule and a longer count in bad conditions.

q: How many points does Alabama assess for speeding 26 mph or more over the limit?
exp: Speeding 1 to 25 mph over is 2 points; 26 mph or more is 5 points.

q: What is Alabama's speed limit on an unpaved road when no other limit is posted?
exp: The statutory limit on an unpaved road is 35 mph.

q: What is Alabama's speed limit on a paved county road unless another limit is posted?
exp: Paved county roads have a 45 mph limit unless posted otherwise.

q: What is the highest speed limit that may be posted on an Alabama interstate?
exp: The statutory list allows 70 mph where posted on interstates.

q: How many points does Alabama assess for speeding 10 mph over the limit?
exp: Speeding 1 to 25 mph over the limit is a 2-point violation.

q: In bad weather or on poor roads, how much following distance does the Alabama manual recommend?
exp: Increase to a four or five second count when road or weather conditions are poor.

q: How many points does following too closely add to an Alabama record?
exp: Following too closely is a 3-point violation.

q: Where a minimum speed is posted on an Alabama highway, driving below it in normal conditions is:
exp: Any speed below a posted minimum is unlawful under normal conditions.

q: On an Alabama interstate, how far may you stay in the left lane without passing another vehicle, in normal traffic?
exp: Alabama's anti-road-rage law bars staying in the left lane more than 1.5 consecutive miles without passing.
src: ALEA news release, Three Traffic Laws Effective Sunday, Sept. 1 (Act 2019-515)

q: What does a steady red X over a lane mean in Alabama?
a: The lane is for carpools only
b: Do not drive in that lane
c: Slow down and use the lane
exp: A driver facing a steady red X must not drive in the lane under it.

q: What does a steady green arrow over a lane mean in Alabama?
a: Turn left from that lane only
c: You may drive in that lane
d: The lane is reserved for emergency vehicles
exp: A steady green arrow permits driving in the lane over which it is shown.

q: Which of these is an exception to Alabama's left lane limit on interstates?
b: Listening to directions on your phone
d: Getting ready to exit on the left
exp: Exceptions include traffic and weather conditions, exiting to the left, paying a toll and emergency vehicles.
src: ALEA news release, Three Traffic Laws Effective Sunday, Sept. 1 (Act 2019-515)

q: In Alabama, how close to a fire hydrant may you park?
exp: Parking is not allowed within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.

q: In Alabama, how close to a stop sign at the side of the road may you park?
exp: Parking is banned within 30 feet of a flashing beacon, stop sign or traffic signal at the roadside.

q: In Alabama, how close to the nearest rail of a railroad crossing may you park?
exp: Parking is not allowed within 50 feet of the nearest rail.

q: In Alabama, how close to a crosswalk at an uncontrolled intersection may you park?
exp: Parking is not allowed within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an uncontrolled intersection.

q: Which curb color means no parking in Alabama?
exp: Do not park beside a curb painted yellow.

q: Your car breaks down on a rural Alabama highway. What does the law require?
a: Leave it in the lane with the hood up
b: Move it off the pavement, or use lights and markers if you cannot
c: Stay in the car with the engine running
d: Leave it where it stopped until morning
exp: A vehicle left standing on a rural highway must be moved off the main traveled part, or marked and lit.

q: How much space does Alabama law require when you pass a person on a bicycle?
exp: Pass a person on a bicycle with no less than three feet between your vehicle and the rider.

q: Under Alabama law, bicycle riders under what age must wear a helmet?
exp: Riders under 16 must wear a securely fastened helmet on public roads, paths and parks.

q: May people on bicycles ride two abreast in Alabama?
b: Only on roads without lane lines
exp: Alabama law allows people on bicycles to ride two abreast at all times.

q: When may an Alabama driver enter a marked bicycle lane?
a: To pass slow traffic on the right
b: Any time no cyclist is in sight
d: To park where allowed, to enter or leave the road, or to prepare for a turn
exp: Drivers may use a bike lane only to park where parking is allowed, enter or leave the road, or prepare to turn.

q: Is it legal for people to ride bicycles on the sidewalk in Alabama?
exp: The manual says it is illegal for people on bicycles to ride on the sidewalk.

q: Within how many feet of an oncoming vehicle must an Alabama driver switch to low beams?
exp: Dim your headlights within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle and within 200 feet when following.

q: When must Alabama drivers have their headlights on?
b: From half an hour after sunset to half an hour before sunrise
c: From sunset to sunrise only on highways
exp: Headlights are required from a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise and when you cannot see 500 feet.

q: After a crash in Alabama with $500 or more in damage, when must form SR-31 be sent to ALEA?
b: Only if police did not come
c: Within 30 days, if the at-fault driver had no insurance
d: Within one year, if anyone was hurt
exp: With injury, death or $500+ damage, an SR-31 is due within 30 days if the at-fault party was uninsured.

q: Within how many feet of a vehicle you are following must an Alabama driver use low beams?
exp: You must dim your lights within 200 feet when following another vehicle.

q: Alabama requires headlights whenever you cannot see clearly for at least how far?
exp: Headlights are required in limited visibility when you cannot see clearly for at least 500 feet.

q: When does Alabama law require headlights because of your windshield wipers?
b: When the wipers are in use because of rain, sleet or snow
c: Only when wipers run on high speed
d: Never; wipers and lights are not linked
exp: Headlights must be on when wipers are in use for rain, sleet or snow; occasional intermittent use does not count.

q: What number can you dial from a cell phone to reach Alabama State Troopers about a crash or drunk driver?
exp: Dial *HP or *47 toll free to contact Alabama State Troopers.

q: An injury crash happens on a state highway outside any city in Alabama. Whom do you notify?
c: No one, if everyone can walk
exp: Injury or fatal crashes must be reported quickly to local police in a city or to State Troopers on a state highway.

q: During an Alabama traffic stop at night, what does the manual tell you to do?
a: Turn on your vehicle's interior lights
b: Get out and walk to the police car
d: Start looking for your documents right away
exp: At night, turn on interior lights to help the officer, and keep your hands on the wheel.

q: According to the Alabama manual, when should you tell an officer about a weapon in your vehicle?
exp: If there are weapons in the vehicle, inform the officer upon first contact.

q: What does signing an Alabama traffic citation mean?
b: You waive your right to court
c: It is not an admission of guilt
d: You agree to pay a double fine
exp: Signing a citation is not an admission of guilt, but refusing to sign may result in arrest.

q: What is the legal BAC limit for an Alabama driver under 21?
exp: It is unlawful for a person under 21 to drive with a BAC of 0.02 percent or more.
src: Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 33; Code of Ala. 32-5A-191(b)

q: What is the fine for a first hands-free law violation in Alabama?
exp: A first conviction brings a $50 fine and 1 point; later ones within 24 months cost more.
src: Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 16; WBRC, Hands-free law to take effect in Alabama this June (March 12, 2024)

q: What license suspension follows a first Alabama DUI conviction for an adult?
exp: A first conviction brings a 90-day suspension plus a fine of $600 to $2,100 and possible jail.
src: Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 33; Code of Ala. 32-5A-191(e)

q: What is the legal BAC limit for an Alabama commercial vehicle driver?
exp: Commercial vehicle operators may not drive with a BAC of 0.04 percent or more.

q: In Alabama, what happens to the minimum DUI punishment when the driver's BAC is 0.15 or more?
exp: A BAC of 0.15 or more at least doubles the minimum punishment.

q: What is the fine range for a first DUI conviction in Alabama?
exp: A first conviction carries a fine of $600 to $2,100, up to one year in jail, or both.

q: What happens to a driver's license after a second Alabama DUI conviction within 10 years?
b: It is revoked for five years
c: It is revoked for one year
d: Nothing, if the fine is paid
exp: A second conviction in 10 years requires a one-year revocation, plus a fine and jail or community service.

q: A fourth DUI conviction in Alabama is classified as:
exp: A fourth or later conviction is a Class C felony.

q: What happens if you refuse a chemical test after an Alabama DUI arrest?
a: Your license is suspended for at least 90 days
b: Nothing, if you are later found not guilty
exp: Refusing the test brings a suspension of at least 90 days, separate from the DUI case.
src: Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 34; Code of Ala. 32-5-192

q: Under Alabama's open container law, what is the fine for an open alcohol container in the passenger area?
exp: An open container in the passenger area on a public road is punishable by a fine of up to $25.

q: In Alabama, where may an opened bottle of alcohol be carried in a car on a public road?
exp: Open containers are allowed in the trunk or a cargo area, not in the passenger area.

q: What license suspension does a first-time Alabama driver under 21 face for a BAC from 0.02 up to 0.08?
exp: A first violation by an under-21 driver at 0.02 to 0.08 brings a 30-day suspension.

q: An Alabama 19-year-old uses a fake ID to buy beer. Besides a fine, what can happen to their license?
b: Nothing, since no car was involved
exp: Using a false ID or possessing alcohol under 21 carries a mandatory license suspension of 3 to 6 months.
src: Code of Ala. 28-3A-25 (University of Alabama, State and City Alcohol Penalties); Code of Ala. 28-3A-25(a)(18), (a)(21), (b)(2), (c) (law.justia.com/codes/alabama/title-28/chapter-3a/section-28-3a-25/)

q: Under Alabama's hands-free law, which phone use is allowed while driving?
a: Holding the phone to read a map
b: Using one tap or swipe to start or end a call
d: Recording a video while moving slowly
exp: Voice and Bluetooth use and a single tap or swipe to start or end a call are allowed.
src: Wetumpka Herald, Alabama enforces amendment to hands-free driving law; Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 16

q: What is the fine for a third Alabama hands-free violation within 24 months?
exp: First $50 and 1 point, second $100 and 2 points, third $150 and 3 points within 24 months.

q: Under Alabama's hands-free law, when is holding a phone while driving a violation?
d: When an officer also sees you swerve, cross lanes without a signal or otherwise drive improperly
exp: Holding a phone is a violation when the driver is also seen crossing lanes without a signal, swerving or otherwise driving improperly.
src: Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 16; Code of Ala. 32-5A-350.1 as quoted in Cullman Tribune, June 6, 2024 (cullmantribune.com/?p=108709)

q: How many points does an Alabama DUI conviction add if it did not require revocation?
exp: Alcohol-related driving convictions not requiring revocation carry 6 points.
src: Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 18 to 19

q: Up to what age must Alabama children ride in a booster seat?
exp: The law requires a booster seat until a child is 6 years old.
src: Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 30; Code of Ala. 32-5-222

q: What are Alabama's minimum liability insurance amounts?
b: $25,000 per person, $50,000 per crash for injury, $25,000 for property
exp: Alabama requires 25/50/25 liability coverage.

q: How many points within two years bring a 60-day suspension in Alabama?
exp: Twelve to 14 points in two years bring a 60-day suspension.

q: Which Alabama vehicle occupants must wear a seat belt?
exp: All occupants must be buckled; a back seat violation is secondary.
src: ALEA news release, Three Traffic Laws Effective Sunday, Sept. 1 (Act 2019-386); Alabama Driver Manual (ALEA, November 2024), p. 30

q: In Alabama, how is a seat belt violation by a back seat passenger enforced?
exp: A belt violation outside the front seat can be cited only after a stop for another violation.
src: Code of Ala. 32-5B-4; ALEA news release (Act 2019-386)

q: Until what minimum age or weight must an Alabama infant ride in a rear-facing seat?
exp: Infants ride rear-facing until at least age 1 or 20 pounds.

q: Until what age does Alabama's child restraint law require a child to be buckled?
exp: Children through age 15 must be restrained in front and back seats.

q: What is the fine for violating Alabama's child restraint law?
exp: The fine is $25 per offense, with 1 point for a first violation and 2 after.

q: What is the minimum legal tire tread depth in Alabama?
exp: A tire is illegal if the tread is less than 1/16 inch deep.

q: How dark may the side windows of an Alabama passenger car be tinted?
a: They must let through at least 70 percent
b: They must let through at least 32 percent of light
exp: Side and rear windows on passenger cars must allow at least 32 percent light transmission.

q: How much of the Alabama windshield may be tinted?
exp: Only the upper 6 inches of the windshield may have transparent tint.

q: How many points does Alabama assess for failure to yield the right of way?
exp: Failure to yield the right of way is a 5-point violation.

q: How long do points count toward an Alabama suspension?
exp: Points count for suspension purposes for two years from the conviction but remain on the record.

q: What is the minimum reinstatement fee after an Alabama license suspension?
exp: Reinstatement costs not less than $100 plus any other requirements.

q: What is the maximum fine for a first Alabama conviction for driving without required liability insurance?
exp: A first violation can bring a fine up to $500; a second up to $1,000 and a possible six-month suspension.

q: Alabama requires rearview mirrors that let the driver see how far to the rear?
exp: Mirrors must let the driver see 200 feet to the rear.

q: On the Alabama road test, how close to the curb must you park on a hill?
exp: The road test hill parking task asks you to park parallel to the curb within 18 inches.

q: Which papers must you show for the car before the Alabama road test?
a: The car's title and bill of sale
b: Proof of insurance and vehicle registration
exp: The applicant must present proof of insurance and vehicle registration.

q: What following distance does the Alabama road test study guide tell you to use?
a: One car length for every 20 mph
exp: The study guide lists following distance using the two-second rule.

q: On the Alabama road test three-point turn, which of these is a mistake?
d: Using a driveway to turn around
exp: Turn around on a narrow street with one backing move, without hitting the curb or using a driveway.

q: Which of these is a reason to fail the Alabama road test at once?
a: Refusing to cooperate with the examiner
c: Stopping fully behind a stop line
exp: Failure to cooperate, a crash, a violation or reckless driving fails you.
